analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell -2.68% last week (+0.31% Friday), its worst week since April 2025. The Philly semiconductor index fell -12.15% (+4.21% Friday) and CoreWeave fell -15.44% (+6.28% Friday).
Rotation within the S&P 500: Consumer Discretionary (+2.68%) and Communication Services (+2.26%) led five of 11 sectors that rose. Energy (-11.93%) fell more than IT (-6.93%).
Japan's Nikkei fell -9.25% last week (-5.96% Friday), its worst week since March 2020. STOXX 600 rose +0.24% (-1.00% Friday), helped by smaller tech exposure and lower oil.

Brent (January 2027 contract) fell -13.32% on the week to $98.32/bbl as fears of Middle East escalation eased. Oil's drop and the AI selloff pulled sovereign yields lower: 10yr UST -7.2bps to 4.86%, 10yr Bund -6.9bps to 3.25%.
October US payrolls rose +165k vs +70k expected, with +84k of upward revisions to the prior two months. The 3-month average is +137k and unemployment fell to 4.1% vs 4.2% expected.
Gold rose +5.06% last week, its best week since August. Credit was flat on both sides of the Atlantic.

October CPI is due tomorrow (Nov 10). DB economists expect headline +0.20% m/m (prior 0.65%) and core +0.20% (prior 0.33%). Year-on-year rates cannot be calculated because October 2025 index levels were not produced during the government shutdown.
October PPI is due Friday. DB expects +0.20% m/m (prior 0.32%), with y/y steady at 3.1%. It is relevant for the core PCE read-across.
About two-thirds of Fed officials speak this week. DB economists still expect 25bp hikes at the December and March FOMC meetings, absent a further material tightening in financial conditions.

Asian markets are rebounding Monday. Taiex +4.94% ended a seven-session losing streak after regulators announced confidence-restoring measures. Nikkei +2.63% and TOPIX +3.20%. Japan and Taiwan equities had both entered bear-market territory last week.
An internal investigation involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is capping gains. Nvidia is down about -3.5% on platforms with weekend prices.
China October PPI rose 5.7% y/y vs 5.0% in September and 5.3% expected, the fastest in nearly 4.5 years, driven by higher global oil prices. CPI rose 0.7% y/y vs 0.9% prior and 0.8% consensus.
UK September GDP is expected at -0.1% m/m on Thursday, with Q3 growth at 0.7% q/q.

Earnings calendar: CoreWeave and SoftBank on Nov 10, Cisco, Applied Materials, Cerebras, Siemens and Allianz on Nov 12. CoreWeave and Cerebras are read-throughs for AI demand and investment. About 90% of S&P 500 companies have reported.

Q3 global earnings growth is likely 33% (38% in Q2). US growth is likely 34%, with the median company at 14%. Europe accelerated from 22% to a four-year high of 28%, and is matching or exceeding US growth in 6 of 11 sectors. Japan is 33% and EM 39%. Estimates are being upgraded, particularly in Korea and Taiwan.
US bond markets are closed Wednesday Nov 11 for Veterans' Day. US auctions: 3-yr $58bn Monday, 10-yr $42bn Tuesday, 30-yr $25bn Thursday.

market_movers.rationale: Shares are down about -3.5% on weekend-pricing platforms. An internal investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang is capping the Asian rebound.
CoreWeave fell -15.44% last week and reports Nov 10. DB flags it as a read on AI demand and investment.

earnings_insights: Q3 global earnings growth is likely 33% y/y (estimate by DB asset allocation), vs 38% in Q2. Growth ex Tech, Energy and Materials is about 12%.
Q3 US earnings growth is likely 34% y/y (DB estimate), median company +14%, ex Tech/Energy/Materials +13%. Close to 90% of S&P 500 companies have reported.
Q3 Europe earnings growth likely 28% y/y (DB estimate), up from 22% and a four-year high. Japan likely 33% and EM 39%.

Upcoming reports: KKR (Nov 9), SoftBank, CoreWeave, Petrobras, Infineon, TransDigm, Vodafone, Venture Global (Nov 10), Cisco, Applied Materials, Siemens, Allianz, Cerebras, Nebius (Nov 12). No consensus figures are given.

Further Fed hikes priced for 2026 stand at 19bp (+2bp) and ECB hikes at 20bp (unch).
